title: Route scalar callers through existing SIMD dispatch
description:
Quick wins (V0→V3 in one hop) where the SIMD kernel already exists in `gf2-kernels-simd` but the scalar caller never dispatches through it. ## Children (3 tasks) - **A1** — `BitMatrix::matvec` (`crates/gf2-core/src/matrix.rs:962-988`): scalar `count_ones() % 2` per row → route through `simd::maybe_simd().popcnt_fn` for rows above a width threshold. - **A2** — `BitMatrix::mul` non-M4RM path (`crates/gf2-core/src/matrix.rs:1165+`): scalar inner-product → route row-XOR through `LogicalFns::xor_fn`. - **A3** — `gfp::FieldVec` add/sub/mul fallback for `Fp

` not in `{65537, 2^31-1}` (`crates/gf2-core/src/gfp/simd_ops.rs`): extend the `SimdVecOps` dispatch to a generic Solinas-friendly form before the scalar fallback. ## Why this story exists The SIMD kernels already exist; the only work is wiring + bench + asm verify. Highest-ROI tasks in the epic. ## Depends on S0 (all four I-tasks). ## Success criteria - [hard] Each task ships per the per-kernel execution protocol in the epic spec doc (baseline saved, asm inspected, perf-stat captured, proptest equivalence, ≥1.5× geomean). - [hard] No `unsafe` introduced outside `gf2-kernels-simd`.
